report:
**Conclusion:** Extensive scientific and clinical evidence demonstrates that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks does **not** cause dangerous carbon-dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup (hypercapnia) or oxygen deprivation in healthy individuals.

### Key Evidence and Physiology
* **Gas Permeability:** $\text{CO}_2$ gas molecules are sub-nanometer in size, making them infinitely smaller than the microscopic pores in cloth fabrics and surgical mask filters. Exhaled $\text{CO}_2$ freely diffuses through the mask and escapes around its loose edges.
* **Physiological Measurements:** Systematic reviews and clinical studies measuring end-tidal $\text{CO}_2$ and blood oxygen saturation confirm that wearing surgical or cloth masks during rest or light exercise does not significantly impair gas exchange or alter blood gas levels.
* **Discomfort vs. Danger:** Although masks can create thermal discomfort, moisture, or a subjective feeling of breathlessness, health authorities (including the CDC) confirm these sensations are psychological or physical reactions to heat, not symptoms of hypercapnia or gas retention.

### Sources
* USA Today Fact Check: https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/
* Health Desk Analysis: https://health-desk.org/articles/does-exhaled-carbon-dioxide-in-a-mask-cause-any-side-effects
* Science Feedback Expert Review: https://science.feedback.org/review/wearing-face-masks-does-not-cause-hypercapnia-or-affect-the-immune-system/
* Systematic Review on Masking and $\text{CO}_2$ (NCBI): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11386028/
